name: UALink 200G 1.0
bandwidth_basis: PER LANE, PER DIRECTION. The consortium states the 200G 1.0 specification 'enables 200G per lane scale-up connection'. UALink reuses IEEE 802.3 PAM4 SerDes, so 200G is a per-lane line rate in each direction and the recorded value is that per-lane per-direction rate. link_count 16 is the consortium's standard 16-lane scale-up port width and is recorded as the typical fabric port width rather than a vendor-confirmed link count - see notes. There is NO published x16 or per-GPU aggregate for UALink, so none is recorded here; a per-pod aggregate must not be inferred from the lane rate alone without a port width.
topology: Multi-layer fabric (UPLI protocol / transaction / data link / physical). Consortium-supported topologies: mesh and ring for small clusters of 4-16 nodes, torus for mid-scale, SWITCHED POD as the primary deployment model scaling to hundreds or thousands of accelerators, and direct-attach for small clusters. Complex ring and torus topologies are explicitly out of specification scope and need care to avoid deadlocks.
switching: Switches are the primary scale-up model, as opposed to NVLink's NVSwitch which is a vendor-specific companion. Common 2.0 adds In-Network Compute, letting reduction traffic be processed between accelerators rather than only at endpoints.
notes: The open scale-up standard: an alternative to NVLink, positioned as deterministic, lossless, sub-microsecond round-trip, reusing commodity Ethernet PAM4 economics. Inference consequence and current status: this is a SPECIFICATION, not a shipping product line. The white paper states UALink 200G 1.0 was published April 2025 and that switch evaluation hardware is expected late 2026, with multiple vendors developing switches, retimers, connectors and transport engines. As of the access date there is no production silicon, so no measured inference number can reference UALink. Consortium reports 115+ member companies including AMD, Apple, AWS, Cisco, Google, Intel, Meta, Microsoft and Alibaba. Stated efficiency is 93% protocol payload over physical-layer capacity, 64-256 byte transactions, and a 57-bit physical address space supporting 128 PB directly addressable. The strategy significance is that a multi-vendor scale-up option removes NVIDIA's single-vendor hold on tensor parallelism, which is why it matters even with no silicon. Verification caveat: the 200 Gb/s lane rate and the 1,024 accelerator pod limit are consortium-stated; the port-width figure in link_count is the weakest claim in this record.
